validity.recommendation: Rename row to 'Karawan Gas Pipeline' (or similar), correct StartLocation/EndLocation region from 'Western Desert' to offshore Temsah Concession / East Nile Delta (Mediterranean, near Port Said) — NOT Western Desert — and re-verify Owner (probably not '100% General Petroleum Co').
validity.researcher_notes: This row is misidentified. GEM's own gem.wiki page (https://www.gem.wiki/Qarun_Gas_Pipeline, read for leads only, not cited) gives the pipeline's Arabic name as انبوب فاز حقل كروان = 'gas pipeline of the Karawan field' (كروان = Karawan), NOT قارون (Qarun) — these are two unrelated Arabic words that were conflated in translation. 'Qarun' is a real, well-documented, entirely distinct entity: Qarun Petroleum Company (QPC) is an EGPC/Apache Corporation joint venture producing OIL in the Qarun concession, Western Desert (verified: gulfoilandgas.com/webpro1/prod1/suppliercat.asp?sid=2806, contains 'Qarun' + 'Apache' — OK); QPC's own real pipeline is a 45 km, 16-inch OIL line to Dahshour, nothing like this row's 206 km/10 in gas spec. 'Karawan' (كروان), by contrast, is an offshore Mediterranean gas field in the Temsah Concession (East Nile Delta, ~60 km off Port Said, ~68 m water depth), developed jointly with the Denise field under Eni/BP's 'DEKA' (Denise-Karawan) project, operated by the Petrobel joint venture (Petrobel = Belayim Petroleum Company — matches this row's Operator field). Independent English trade press (egyptoil-gas.com DEKA feature, verified OK; offshore-mag.com DEKA article, verified OK) confirms: 'The DEKA project launched by Petrobel is targeting the development of both the Denise and Karawan fields' in the 'Temsah Concession located at offshore Egypt.' The sheet's own existing Length/Diameter ref (almalnews.com/9021, verified OK, contains 'كروان' and '206') explicitly attaches the 206 km/10 in figures to the KARAWAN project, not Qarun — confirming the data values were pulled correctly but the identity/name/location were not. This also means the row's Status/Fuel/PipelineType ref (petro-news.com/95212/, a roundup of '39 gas projects in Egypt') does not mention Qarun OR Karawan by name at all (checked directly — lists 8 unrelated trunk lines: Idku-Abu Hamsa, Nobaria-Mit Nama, Dahshur-Al Wasati, Tina-Abu Sultan, New Capital-Dahshur, Nors-Abu Madi-El Gamil, Nobaria-Sadat, Gamsa-Finosa), matching the worklist's own automated flag ('200 but data value not found'). Net: the underlying pipe (a Karawan-field subsea sealine tying into the existing 32-inch Denise/Temsah export network to El Gamil) does physically exist and is well corroborated — but under the WRONG name and WRONG location in this GEM row. Owner is also suspect: 'General Petroleum Co (GPC)' is a different EGPC subsidiary (Gulf of Suez-oriented); the Temsah Concession / DEKA project is a 50/50 Eni-BP interest operated via Petrobel — GPC as 100% owner does not match any source found and should be re-verified, not left as-is.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify the 206 km length against DEKA project engineering literature before treating it as confirmed; likely too long by an order of magnitude for a field-to-existing-line tie-in at this distance offshore.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Length=206 km / Diameter=10 in traces to almalnews.com/9021 (Arabic), which states the Karawan project pipeline is 'بطول 206 كم وقطر 10 بوصات' (206 km long, 10 in diameter) tying into the existing 32-inch sealine. That is the ONLY source for this number, and it is a single, non-independently-corroborated figure (tier=low per the confidence rubric — no second source agrees). It is also hard to reconcile with the physical geography and with independent English technical trade coverage of the same DEKA project: the Karawan field itself is only ~60 km off the Egyptian coast (egyptoil-gas.com DEKA feature, verified OK), and that same feature states the ENTIRE DEKA project (both Denise and Karawan fields combined) laid only '4 gas sealines (9 km 16" & 4 km 10") and relevant tie-ins to [the] 32" existing sealine network' — i.e. a maximum of ~13 km of new small-diameter sealine project-wide, not 206 km for Karawan alone. A 206 km, 10-inch tie-in from a field only ~60 km offshore is not plausible as described. Possible explanations: a decimal-point transcription error in the original Arabic source (e.g. 20.6 km), a mix-up with a cumulative/different length figure, or conflation with the separately-listed Denise-project figures (3.7 km, 405 km, 1 km) from the same almalnews article (GEM already has a 'Denise Gas Pipeline', P7447, at 405 km/16in from this same article — also worth an independent re-check, as 405 km is equally implausible for a ~70 km-offshore tie-in). Recommend treating 206 km as unresolved/low-confidence pending a second, independent source (e.g. an SPE/OnePetro engineering paper on DEKA) rather than confirmed.

fills.researcher_notes: Operator = Belayim Petroleum Co (Petrobel, the common short name for Belayim Petroleum Company, the Eni/EGPC-BP joint operating company). Two independent English trade sources confirm Petrobel operates the DEKA (Denise-Karawan) development this pipeline actually belongs to: egyptoil-gas.com ('The DEKA project launched by Petrobel is targeting the development of both the Denise and Karawan fields') and offshore-mag.com's DEKA production-start article. Note: this Operator value is correct for the underlying Karawan-field pipeline even though the row's name/location (Qarun / Western Desert) is wrong — see validity findings; the Operator fill is issued independent of that naming problem since it matches the real facility this row's Length/Diameter values describe.

routes.start_name: Karawan gas field (offshore, Temsah Concession, East Nile Delta / Mediterranean Sea)
routes.end_name: Existing 32-inch Denise/Temsah export sealine tie-in feeding the El Gamil gas plant near Port Said, Egypt

waypoints.name: Port Said, Egypt (shore reference point; El Gamil gas terminal lies just west of the city)

routes.corridor_desc: Per egyptoil-gas.com's DEKA feature (verified) and the BP/Eni project descriptions, the Karawan field sits roughly 60 km off the Egyptian coast in the Temsah Concession, East Nile Delta, at about 68 m water depth, and is developed jointly with the nearby Denise field under the Petrobel-operated DEKA project. New subsea sealines from the Karawan/Denise wells tie into the existing 32-inch offshore export network that runs to the El Gamil gas processing plant near Port Said. I could not source a precise field wellhead coordinate, so start_lat/start_lon are left null rather than guessed; Port Said is given only as a defensible, named shore anchor for the tie-in end, not the field itself. This is a loose corridor bound (offshore box roughly north/NNE of Port Said out to ~60-70 km), not a route line — a human routes-repo pass would need an SPE/OnePetro field-development paper or a GEBCO/concession map to tighten it.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the DEKA project's own field-location description (Karawan field, Temsah Concession, ~60 km offshore, ~68 m water depth) and the fact that all DEKA sealines tie into the existing 32-inch export line feeding El Gamil near Port Said. No fabricated coordinates: field wellhead lat/lon left null; Port Said's real, well-known coordinates are used only as a named shore anchor for the tie-in end, and the corridor is described in words as a loose offshore box rather than a drawn line.

summary: P7572 'Qarun Gas Pipeline' is misidentified: it is actually a mistranslation/conflation of the unrelated 'Karawan' (كروان) offshore gas field — part of the Eni/BP-Petrobel 'DEKA' (Denise-Karawan) project in the Temsah Concession, East Nile Delta — with the real, distinct 'Qarun' (قارون) Western Desert oil JV (Apache/EGPC); location should be offshore Mediterranean near Port Said, not Western Desert, Owner should be re-verified (GPC looks wrong for a Petrobel/Eni-BP asset), and the 206 km length itself is an unresolved single-source figure that looks implausible against the field's ~60 km offshore distance and DEKA's own stated ~13 km of new sealine — route corridor suggested at low confidence pending human review.
